rationale:
All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_reported/trait_efo and phenotyping_reported all indicate abdominal aortic aneurysm), so the decision hinges on comparative PRS evidence quality and study archetype rather than label alignment.

PGS000753 is preferred because it comes from a disease-focused AAA genetics study (Million Veteran Program; Circulation) and, critically, reports a PRS effect size (OR per SD 1.37, 95% CI 1.30–1.44) under basic covariates (age, sex, PCs). Domain guidance treats per-SD OR as a strong, PRS-comparable signal when AUC/R2 are missing, and this model avoids the “framework/portability” penalty that applies to some other candidates.

However, the overall pool has limited directly comparable PRS-only metrics (most candidates report only full-model AUROC/C-index or partial-r), and several newer disease-focused PRS-CS models (PGS003972/PGS003973) are plausible competitors but lack PRS-only R2/OR/HR in the visible fields; their high full-model discrimination (e.g., C-index 0.882 for PGS003973) cannot be treated as PRS-only evidence. This metric incomparability keeps confidence at Moderate and the outcome at DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL.

Runner-up ordering reflects remaining direct-match support after the winner: PGS003973 and PGS003972 are from a large AAA GWAS meta-analysis (Nat Genet) with genome-wide shrinkage (PRS-CS) and coherent disease-focused cohort lists, but rely on full-model metrics with limited covariate transparency; PGS002054 and PGS001784 have explicit PRS-comparable metrics (partial-r ~0.0144; Nagelkerke R2 ~0.0147) but are from portability/framework-style papers, which domain guidance penalizes when disease-focused alternatives exist.

All 4 candidates are direct-match/near-direct for the target (alcohol dependence / alcohol use disorder / problematic alcohol use), with endpoint fidelity primarily supported by phenotyping_reported. PGS002738 is best supported because it is explicitly aligned to alcohol use disorder (trait_efo=alcohol dependence; phenotyping_reported=Alcohol use disorder), is developed in a disease-focused multi-cohort context (MVP, UKB), and reports a reasonably strong discriminative effect size (OR top 10% vs rest=1.96, 95% CI 1.54–2.51) on a sizable EUR evaluation sample (n=7,900). Main limitation: covariates are unknown and there is no PRS-comparable AUC/R2, so ranking relies on effect-size evidence and study context.

Runners-up: PGS000201 is a close alternative with strong endpoint fidelity (DSM-5 AUD criteria count) and the largest genome-wide PRS-CS variant count (~1.09M) plus a PRS-specific incremental ΔR²=0.01192 (below the provided EUR h2_obs=0.036 ceiling), but it is UKB-only development and reports weaker effect-size evidence than PGS002738. PGS002739 is endpoint-aligned (AUD; trait_efo alcohol dependence) and shows OR top 10% vs rest=1.76 in an AFR evaluation (n=6,315), but its gene-based sparse construction (858 variants) and non-EUR-only evaluation make it less safe as a general top-5 pick absent a specified deployment ancestry. PGS000202 is the weakest of the sibling UKB PRS-CS scores due to smaller validation (n=1,251) and lower incremental ΔR²=0.00456 with a less compelling beta estimate.

Direct-match candidates present (3) and all map to the target EFO. Best-supported is PGS001777 because it is explicitly alcohol-related cirrhosis and provides the most PRS-informative discrimination signal among the set via a large stratification effect (OR top 20% vs bottom 20% = 6.18) plus an AUROC (0.671) in European evaluation; this is more directly interpretable as PRS contribution than PGS000704’s full-model C-index (0.711) which is explicitly covariate-adjusted and lacks PGS-only/incremental metrics. PGS004913 is a close runner-up with endpoint-aligned phenotyping and an R²=0.029 plus OR top vs bottom deciles=4.4, but its evidence is limited by smaller training/validation sizes and the R² is not explicitly labeled as PGS-only vs full-model. PGS000704 ranks behind because it appears to come from a broad biomarker genetics context and reports only full-model discrimination (C-index 0.711) with no PRS-only AUC/R², making its apparent performance harder to attribute to the PRS. Overall confidence is low because none of the candidates reports clearly PRS-only AUROC/R² and the reported metrics are not fully comparable across studies (full-model vs unclear R² vs small-cohort AUROC), so the #1 choice is uncertain under the provided ranking policy. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All 19 candidates are direct matches to angina pectoris by trait_efo, with generally acceptable endpoint fidelity (ICD10 I20, PheCode 411.3, or angina diagnosis/self-report variants). The strongest visible PRS-discrimination evidence comes from the 2024 HGG Adv MVP-based set (PGS005047–PGS005059), which report comparable C-index values (~0.75–0.77) and per-SD ORs; within this coherent family, PGS005052 has the highest reported C-index (0.766245) and a strong per-SD OR (1.491, 95% CI 1.42–1.57), making it the best-supported pick for likely top-5 benchmark safety. Runners-up are selected from the same MVP family with nearly identical endpoint/covariates and the next-highest C-index/OR support: PGS005048 (C-index 0.766876; OR 1.487), PGS005057 (0.766367; OR 1.479), PGS005051 (0.765456; OR 1.455), and PGS005050 (0.765078; OR 1.445). Main limitation: these MVP models lack explicit PRS-only AUROC/R² (only full-model C-index is shown), and several UKB framework scores (PGS001260–PGS001262) report PRS-only AUROC/R² but come from a pan-trait sparse framework and/or show high full-model AUROC likely dominated by covariates with small incremental AUROC, making cross-model comparability and the #1 choice uncertain from the visible evidence alone.

All 9 candidates are direct matches to ankylosing spondylitis by trait_efo and phenotyping_reported, so a direct-match exists. For benchmark-oriented selection, the strongest visible PRS-comparable evidence is from the UKB snpnet models (PGS001267/PGS001268), which uniquely report explicit PGS-only metrics (PGS AUROC no covariates and PGS R2 no covariates) plus incremental AUROC with only basic covariates; their PGS-only R2 (~0.10) is also below the provided liability-scale heritability ceiling (h2_liability~0.399), passing the sanity check. Between the two, PGS001267 is the cleaner endpoint (standard case/control ankylosing spondylitis) versus PGS001268 being time-to-event (explicitly a warning signal in the domain guidance), and their performance is otherwise similar, so PGS001267 is preferred for top-5 safety.

Key limitation: the preferred models come from a known pan-trait UKB framework paper (“across 813 traits”), which the domain guidance flags as often underperforming disease-focused scores in external validation; however, no clearly disease-focused multi-cohort AS PRS is present in this candidate list. Several alternatives have weaker or less comparable performance evidence: the UKB portability scores (PGS002089, PGS001876) report only partial correlation (no PRS-only AUROC/R2), and the Taiwanese EAS-only models (PGS003420 etc.) report only full-model AUROC with unknown covariates and small validation n=1,298, making their apparent AUROC less comparable. Runners-up are therefore ranked by remaining direct-match support: PGS001268 next (similar metrics but TTE endpoint penalty), then PGS002089 (genome-wide LDpred2 with higher partial-r than PGS001876), then PGS001876, then the best of the small EAS-only set by reported full-model AUROC (PGS003420).

Direct-match candidates for the target trait (aortic stenosis) are present: PGS005252, PGS005254, PGS005255, PGS005256. The other returned models (PGS000739/PGS000778/PGS004910/PGS004911) are for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and are not direct matches.

PGS005252 is best supported within the direct-match set because it has the cleanest endpoint alignment (phenotyping_reported: incident aortic stenosis cases; trait_reported/efo: aortic stenosis), a modern genome-wide method (LDPred2) with very large variant count (1,119,377), and the strongest visible risk-gradient evidence among the aortic-stenosis-labeled models (HR=1.92). It also reports a high full-model C-index (0.87), but per the provided domain guidance this is discounted as PRS-comparable evidence because it is a full-model metric and includes multiple clinical covariates; still, it is not obviously a risk-wrapper or biomarker-heavy package.

Runners-up are ranked by remaining direct-match support: PGS005254 is the closest competitor (same disease endpoint; genome-wide PRS-CS; large variant count; HR=1.64 with CI), but it lacks any reported discrimination metric and shows a weaker effect size than PGS005252. PGS005255 and PGS005256 are less directly aligned because their trait_reported are valve-function measurements (mean pressure gradient / peak aortic velocity) even though phenotyping_reported is still incident aortic stenosis; both have similar HR=1.53 and similarly limited metric reporting, making them weaker and largely tied.

Confidence is Moderate because all direct-match candidates lack PRS-only AUROC/R² (so full-model metrics are not directly comparable), and three of the four aortic-stenosis-family scores are near-clones with limited differentiating evidence beyond HR and method label. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

Direct-match candidates for the target trait (arthritis) are present, but the evidence is not strong enough to make a high-confidence #1 pick. PGS001135 is the most endpoint-faithful direct match (trait_efo=arthritis; phenotyping_reported='Arthritis (nos)') and provides PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.53928; PGS-only R2=0.00291; incremental AUROC=0.00314) with standard demographic/PC covariates, making it the cleanest directly comparable arthritis PRS in the visible list. However, its PRS-only performance is weak and the reported local heritability ceiling for arthritis is low (h2_obs≈0.0009; h2_liability≈0.061), so the small PRS-only R2 and incremental AUROC limit confidence that it will rank #1 in an external benchmark.

Runners-up are other direct-match arthritis models but with weaker or less comparable evidence: PGS004547 and PGS004477 both target 'M13 (Other arthritis)' (trait_efo=arthritis) but report only an OR (no PRS-only AUROC/R2) and have unknown covariates, reducing comparability; they are still plausible because they are direct-match and use genome-wide LDpred2/metaPRS-style constructions. PGS001290 (osteoarthritis) and PGS001110 (reactive arthritis) are included as remaining higher-support arthritis-spectrum direct matches in the candidate list, but they are not the generic arthritis endpoint and are from the same pan-trait UKB framework family with limited PRS-only signal for arthritis-like endpoints, lowering top-5 safety.

All listed candidates are direct matches to asthma (trait_efo=asthma), but they vary in endpoint fidelity, PRS-comparable performance evidence, and study archetype. PGS001344 is best supported because it has a clear, clinically anchored endpoint ("Asthma diagnosed by doctor"), reports PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.64568; PGS-only R2=0.05973) plus full-model AUROC=0.66621 with only basic covariates (age/sex/PCs/array), and its PRS-only R2 remains below the provided asthma liability-scale heritability ceiling (h2_liability=0.1515), making the performance evidence internally plausible. Key limitation: it comes from a pan-trait UKB framework paper ("across 813 traits"), which domain guidance flags as often underperforming disease-focused scores in external validation; however, within the visible list it still has the strongest combination of endpoint fidelity and PRS-only metrics.

Runners-up: PGS001782 (PRS-CS-auto; multi-biobank/global framework) has supportive PRS-comparable evidence (Nagelkerke R2 covariates-regressed-out=0.048844; AUROC=0.659) and broad training cohorts, but lacks explicit PGS-only AUROC and is framework-derived. PGS002727 (pediatric asthma; PRS-CS) has very strong effect-size evidence (OR per SD=1.57) and extremely large evaluation n, but its endpoint is pediatric-specific and covariates are unknown, reducing generic-asthma deployment fidelity. PGS002061 and PGS001849 (UKB portability paper) provide coherent PRS signal via partial correlation (0.1184 and 0.1135, respectively) with decent EUR evaluation, but they lack clearer PRS-only AUROC/R2 and come from a portability framework, making them less safe than the best pick despite reasonable structural properties (LDpred2 and penalized regression). | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All 6 candidates are direct-match at the EFO level (atopic eczema), but endpoint fidelity differs materially. PGS002755 is preferred because its phenotyping is closest to the generic target ("Incident atopic dermatitis"), it uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS; 1,090,702 variants) consistent with stronger capture of polygenic signal, and it reports a PRS-associated effect size (HR high vs low PRS 1.249, EUR eval, very large n=337,910). The main limitation is that it does not report PRS-only AUROC/R², so performance comparability is limited and selection relies on structural/method and endpoint alignment.

Runners-up: PGS004587 has the same incident AD endpoint and similarly large EUR validation (n=337,910) but is a sparse 23-variant GWS score with a weaker reported HR (1.153), making it less likely to be top-performing. PGS001773 reports very high full-model AUROC/R² (0.93/0.49) but these are full-model metrics (not PRS-only) and appear implausibly high relative to the provided heritability ceiling (h2_liability≈0.129), plus it targets a narrower subtype (moderate-to-severe AD) with a small validation (n=676), so its apparent advantage is likely non-comparable/covariate-driven. PGS003459 and PGS003486 are further penalized because their phenotyping is therapy-context-specific (paradoxical eczema in biologic-treated psoriasis), making them weaker direct matches to generic atopic eczema despite modest AUROCs (~0.58) and ORs.

All listed candidates are direct matches to atrial fibrillation (or AF/flutter) by trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported, so selection hinges on endpoint fidelity plus PRS-comparable evidence and study archetype. PGS005168 is best supported because it comes from a disease-focused, large multi-cohort AF meta-analysis (Nat Genet 2025) with a direct AF endpoint and basic covariates (age/sex/PCs/array plus CHARGE-AF adjustment noted), and it reports strong discrimination evidence (C-index 0.8718 with CI; HR per SD 1.6663; many performance records), making it the most likely to be a top external performer among the visible direct-match set. Main limitation: the headline C-index is a full-model metric (not explicitly PGS-only), and inclusion of CHARGE-AF in covariates is a risk-wrapper/clinical-calculator signal that can inflate full-model discrimination, so true standalone PRS performance is less directly observed.

Runners-up ranked by remaining direct-match support: PGS005313 (Nat Commun 2025; PRS-CSx; direct AF; strong OR 1.82 with tight CI; clean/basic covariates; multi-cohort development including MVP/UKB/deCODE; but only one record and AUROC likely full-model), PGS002814 (Nat Genet 2023; very large cross-ancestry GWAS; AF endpoint; strong OR ~1.94 and pseudo-R2 0.14 in EAS eval; but evaluation is EAS-only and method is P+T), PGS000016 (Nat Genet 2019; LDpred genome-wide; reports PRS-only Nagelkerke R2=0.029 which is interpretable and below the provided h2 ceiling; large UKB validation; but older and largely UKB-centric), and PGS000331 (Nat Med 2020; LDpred; incident AF; HR 1.62; reasonable C-index 0.751; multi-cohort dev; but smaller training n and less direct PRS-only metric evidence). | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All 4 candidates are direct matches at the concept level (atrial flutter is explicitly present in trait_efo for all; PGS001263 is the only exact atrial-flutter-only endpoint, while the others are atrial fibrillation+flutter composites). However, all candidates come from UK Biobank framework-style papers (either the pan-trait sparse snpnet set or the UKB portability sweep), which domain guidance flags as tending to underperform disease-focused models in external validation; since no disease-focused multi-cohort alternative is present, selection must be made within this limited set.

PGS001263 is preferred because it has the cleanest endpoint fidelity for the target (phenotyping_reported and trait_reported are atrial flutter) and it reports PRS-comparable metrics (PGS AUROC no covariates=0.617 and PGS R2 no covariates=0.025), enabling a more comparable assessment than the portability models that only report partial-r. Its PRS-only R2 is also below the provided heritability ceiling (h2_obs=0.0157; h2_liability=0.1443), so it is not obviously implausible.

Runners-up: PGS001339 is very similar (same snpnet framework, similar PRS-only metrics) but has weaker endpoint fidelity due to time-to-event AF+flutter rather than flutter-only. Between the two portability models, PGS002050 (LDpred2, genome-wide 554,908 variants) is structurally stronger than PGS001841 (penalized regression, 3,980 variants) and has slightly higher partial-r (0.1034 vs 0.1026), so it ranks ahead; both are limited by lacking PRS-only AUROC/R2. Overall confidence is low because the candidate pool is small, all are framework-derived, and the metric types are not fully comparable across the two publication families.

Direct-match candidates present (2). PGS000327 is best supported because its phenotype fields are coherent and directly aligned (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all “Autism spectrum disorder”), it comes from a disease-focused ASD GWAS publication context (Nat Genet: “Identification of common genetic risk variants for autism spectrum disorder.”), and it reports supportive PRS signal in evaluation (OR per SD 1.33 with CI 1.30–1.36; variance explained R²=0.0245) with basic covariates (genetic PCs, genotyping wave) in EUR evaluation (n=7,148). By contrast, PGS002790 has an explicit endpoint/phenotype mismatch (phenotyping_reported “Psychiatric behavior (withdrawn)” despite ASD trait labels), weaker reported metric (partial R²≈0.00546), and lacks training sample size information, making it a riskier direct-match choice despite using a genome-wide shrinkage method (SDPR) and many variants. Overall confidence is Moderate because the pool is small and neither model reports clearly PRS-only AUC/R²; additionally, PGS000327’s reported R² appears to be a full-model metric (full_model_r2), limiting strict PRS-only comparability.

All 20 visible candidates are direct matches to basal cell carcinoma by trait_reported/trait_efo, but endpoint fidelity differs: most Cancer PRSweb models use a direct “Basal cell carcinoma” phenotype, while newer Nat Commun 2023 models (PGS003416/PGS003417) use a broader “Keratinocyte cancers” phenotyping_reported and the 2025 Nat Med model (PGS005207) is explicitly restricted to “risk of basal cell carcinoma in childhood cancer survivors” with treatment/exposure covariates, making them less comparable for generic BCC risk.

Within the strongest endpoint-faithful cluster (Cancer PRSweb, EUR throughout, basic covariates age/sex/batch/PCs), PGS000452 has the strongest visible PRS-discrimination evidence: highest reported per-SD effect size (OR=1.663, 95% CI 1.57–1.761) and the strongest reported pseudo-R² (Nagelkerke’s 0.0487) alongside a high full-model AUROC (0.632). Several close siblings (PGS000454/PGS000456/PGS000458) have nearly identical AUROC (~0.628–0.632) and similar ORs (~1.63–1.66) and pseudo-R² (~0.0456–0.0489), so the #1 choice is not unequivocal; however, PGS000452’s combination of top OR and near-top AUROC/R² provides the broadest mutually consistent support.

Runners-up are ranked by remaining direct-match support within the same endpoint-faithful, clean-covariate set: PGS000454 (essentially tied on AUROC and slightly higher pseudo-R² 0.0489 but marginally lower OR), then PGS000456 and PGS000458 (very similar AUROC/OR with slightly lower pseudo-R²). PGS000730 is included as the next safest alternative due to large independent evaluation (n=88,924) and strong OR (1.57), but it has unknown covariates and lacks comparable PRS-only metrics, lowering certainty.

Main limitation: none of the candidates report explicit PRS-only AUROC/R²; most reported AUROCs are full-model with covariates, so fine-grained ranking among the top Cancer PRSweb siblings remains uncertain, keeping confidence at Moderate. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

Direct-match candidates are present (3 total) and all map to the target EFO concept (bilirubin metabolism disease), but the evidence is insufficient to make a clearly high-quality #1 choice because two of the three candidates lack PRS-comparable AUC/R2 and the remaining candidate’s unusually high reported metrics appear inconsistent with the provided heritability sanity-check.

Best pick: PGS002032 is preferred because it has the strongest structural properties among the endpoint-faithful options: same reported endpoint as PGS001824 (“Disorders of bilirubin excretion”), same training/validation context (UKB portability study; DEV EUR; multi-ancestry EVAL), but uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with a much larger variant set (19,768 vs 22). Under the provided domain guidance, within the same endpoint/publication family and absent differentiating PRS-only AUC/R2, the stronger shrinkage method and higher variant count are the most defensible tie-breakers for expected external performance.

Runners-up: (1) PGS001824 is the closest sibling to the best model (same endpoint and study family) but with a much smaller variant set and penalized regression; it reports the same partial-r as PGS002032, so there is no metric-based reason to rank it above the LDpred2 genome-wide model. (2) PGS000924 is a broader composite endpoint (“Disorders of porphyrin and bilirubin metabolism”) and time-to-event, from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework (snpnet, 5 variants). Although it reports high AUC/R2 and incremental AUROC, those PRS-only R2 values (0.218) exceed the provided local h2_obs (~0.089), triggering the domain ‘heritability ceiling’ concern and making the performance evidence potentially non-comparable or otherwise unreliable; additionally, the framework/sparse-model context is explicitly warned as prone to poorer external generalization.

Main limitation driving low confidence: the two ‘bilirubin excretion’ models provide only partial correlation (partial-r ~0.072) without PRS-only AUC/R2, while the only model with explicit PRS-only metrics (PGS000924) has multiple red flags (framework origin, extreme sparsity, and heritability-ceiling inconsistency). This leaves the #1 choice dependent on structural heuristics rather than clean, comparable performance evidence.

All three candidates are direct lexical/EFO matches to the bipolar disorder spectrum (bipolar disorder, bipolar I, bipolar II) and share the same publication family, method (SDPR), EUR-only GWAS/EVAL ancestry, similar genome-wide variant counts (~935k–949k), similar basic covariates (age, PCs1-3), and similarly small reported full-model partial R² (~0.0025–0.0031). However, endpoint fidelity is weak/indirect for all three because phenotyping_reported reflects non-diagnosis outcomes (cognitive function / DSM5 depression behavior / sluggish cognitive tempo) rather than bipolar disorder case-control status, making the performance metrics hard to interpret for the target trait. With no PRS-only AUC/R² and no effect sizes, the only differentiators are minor and likely noisy; PGS002786 is selected as best mainly because it is the only model labeled exactly 'Bipolar disorder' (closest concept match) and has the largest variant count, but this is insufficient for a high-quality recommendation given the phenotype mismatch and limited comparable performance evidence.

Direct-match set contains 3 candidates. Two (PGS001826, PGS002034) are tightly endpoint-aligned to a specific coagulation disorder subtype ("Congenital deficiency of other clotting factors (including factor VII)", EFO: congenital vitamin K-dependent coagulation factors deficiency), while PGS001033 targets a broader but time-to-event endpoint ("Other coagulation defects (time-to-event)") mapped to the umbrella EFO blood coagulation disease.

PGS002034 is selected as best because, within the same publication family and identical endpoint/covariate/ancestry context as PGS001826 (same UKB portability paper; DEV EUR-only; EVAL EUR/SAS; same covariates; similar partial-r), it has a much larger variant count (32,552 vs 45) and uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) rather than penalized regression with a small SNP set—structural signals that are typically favorable when other evidence is essentially indistinguishable. 

Main limitation: all three candidates come from framework-style UKB-wide studies ("across 813 traits" sparse snpnet; "Portability of 245 polygenic scores"), not clearly disease-focused coagulation studies, and the two congenital-deficiency models lack PRS-comparable AUROC/R² (only partial correlation), while PGS001033’s reported AUROC includes full-model metrics and a time-to-event phenotype, reducing comparability. With no strong, clean, directly comparable PRS-only discrimination evidence across the set, confidence in the #1 ranking is low and the overall direct-match quality is sub-optimal.

Direct-match candidates are abundant for breast carcinoma. The strongest visible cluster is the 2023 Am J Hum Genet multi-biobank method-benchmark family with phenotype-aligned "Breast cancer" endpoints, covariates explicitly "0" (minimizing covariate-driven inflation concerns), and consistent, PRS-comparable discrimination evidence across multiple methods on the same evaluation setting (EVAL: EUR 67%, SAS 33%; n=48,968). Within that coherent family, PGS004153 (UKBB-EUR.MultiPRS.CV) is best supported because it is an explicit multi-score/ensemble model (a positive structural signal) and also has the highest reported full-model AUROC (0.6625) and among the highest R² (0.0764) with strong per-SD OR (1.83), all on the same endpoint/covariate context as its siblings. Runners-up are the closest siblings with nearly identical endpoint/covariate context and slightly lower AUROC/R²: LDpred2.CV (PGS004040) and LDpred2-auto (PGS004025) are next-best on AUROC/R² and effect sizes; PRS-CS-auto (PGS004083) and megaprs.CV (PGS004069) follow with slightly lower but still strong AUROC/R² and OR/β. Main limitation: the evidence shown is dominated by one study family and uses full-model AUROC/R² fields without explicit PGS-only AUROC/R² labeling in these records, so while the within-family ranking is well-supported, cross-study comparability to other breast-cancer PGS (e.g., older consortium scores, incident-only designs, or covariate-heavy clinical packages) remains uncertain from the visible metadata alone.

All 10 visible candidates are direct matches to celiac disease via trait_efo, but they differ in endpoint fidelity and PRS-comparable performance evidence. PGS000316 is best supported because it targets a direct clinical endpoint (phenotyping_reported: Coeliac disease), is disease-focused (pilot clinical care study rather than a pan-trait/portability framework), and reports strong discrimination (full-model AUROC 0.879 with tight CI) in a very large evaluation sample (n=379,767), giving comparatively strong top-5 safety among the direct-match set. The main limitation is that the reported AUROC is a full-model metric with covariates listed as Unknown (no explicit PGS-only AUROC/R²), so comparability to PRS-only performance is uncertain.

Runners-up: PGS000040 is disease-focused with very high reported AUROC (0.90) but has much smaller validation (n=2,476) and also lacks PRS-only metrics/covariate clarity. PGS001301 provides explicit PRS-only metrics (PGS AUROC 0.8287; PGS R² 0.1422) with standard covariates, but comes from a pan-trait UKB framework paper (penalized sparse scores across 813 traits), which domain guidance flags as systematically less reliable externally than disease-focused models. Among the UKB portability-framework family, PGS002067 (LDpred2) and PGS001856 (penalized regression) have the strongest partial-r evidence (0.1241 and 0.1196, respectively) on the exact celiac disease endpoint, but they still lack AUC/R² and are framework-derived, so they rank behind the more disease-focused candidates.

All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_efo=cervical carcinoma; phenotyping_reported is cervical cancer/incident cervical cancer). For likely external-benchmark #1 selection, PGS003428 is best supported structurally as a disease-focused cervical-phenotype GWAS meta-analysis score using a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred) with very large variant count (2,894,555) and a reported per-SD HR signal (HR=1.33), which together are stronger PRS-quality indicators than small GWAS-hit sets or pan-trait sparse models when PRS-only metrics are largely absent. However, confidence is limited because most candidates report only full-model discrimination (often covariate-influenced) and PGS003428’s reported C-index (0.613) is not directly comparable to PRS-only performance; additionally, some alternatives have much higher full-model AUROC (~0.745–0.768) but those are discounted because they are full-model metrics and/or come from cross-cancer or pan-trait frameworks.

Runner-up ordering: PGS000073 and PGS000784 form a coherent near-clone pair with identical endpoint/covariates and similar HR (~1.21–1.22) and full-model AUROC (~0.745) in a large EUR evaluation (n=211,795), giving strong “top-5 safety” despite being only 10-variant GWAS-hit scores; PGS005165 is a direct-match EAS-only evaluation with moderate HR (1.2) but weaker transportability if benchmark is not EAS; PGS001299 is a pan-trait UKB sparse framework (snpnet, 24 variants) with explicit PGS-only metrics but very small PRS-only signal (PGS AUROC ~0.55; PGS R2 ~0.0026), making it less likely to be top-performing externally than disease-focused alternatives.

All 6 candidates are direct matches to cholelithiasis (some via ICD10 K80 or a closely related composite endpoint including cholecystitis). The strongest visible PRS-comparable performance evidence among the set is from the UKB portability study siblings, where PGS002072 (LDpred2) reports the highest partial correlation (partial-r=0.098, 95% CI 0.0842–0.1117) versus PGS001861 (penalized regression) at partial-r=0.0948, with otherwise identical endpoint (“Cholelithiasis and cholecystitis”), covariates, training cohort (UKB), and evaluation context; LDpred2 is also a genome-wide shrinkage method with very large variant count (428,587), supporting better capture of polygenic signal. However, confidence is limited because (i) the partial-r metric is not directly comparable to PRS-only AUROC/R² and no AUROC/R² are provided for these models, and (ii) other direct-match candidates either come from pan-trait UKB framework (PGS001174; despite having explicit PGS-only AUROC/R² and incremental AUROC, framework origin and time-to-event endpoint are warning signals) or from a risk-factor integration paper with unknown covariates and only modest per-SD ORs (PGS004476/PGS004546), or are EAS-evaluated only with only a beta reported (PGS005150), making cross-candidate performance ranking uncertain. Runners-up are ordered by remaining direct-match support: PGS001861 is nearly tied with PGS002072 but slightly weaker partial-r and smaller methodological/variant-count signal; PGS001174 has the richest PRS-only metric reporting but is penalized by pan-trait framework + TTE endpoint; PGS004546 and PGS004476 are exact ICD10 K80 endpoints with moderate ORs but lack comparable metrics and have unknown covariates.

All 22 candidates are direct EFO matches to chronic kidney disease, but they vary in endpoint fidelity and how PRS-comparable the reported performance is. PGS002237 is best supported because it comes from a disease-focused CKD paper (“Genome-wide polygenic score to predict chronic kidney disease across ancestries”, Nat Med 2022), uses a clinically specific CKD definition (stage 3+; eGFR<45), has large development (n=279,819) and multi-ancestry evaluation, and reports a strong per-SD effect size (OR=1.47, 95% CI 1.32–1.65). Although its AUROC=0.78 is a full-model metric with many clinical covariates (so not PRS-only comparable), the combination of endpoint specificity + disease-focused archetype + strong effect size makes it the safest likely top-5 benchmark pick from the visible list.

Runners-up are ranked by remaining direct-match support: (1) PGS004158 (UKBB-EUR.MultiPRS.CV) has the strongest full-model AUROC among the five-biobank method-comparison cluster (AUROC≈0.592; R²≈0.020) with covariates=0 and a coherent CKD/dialysis endpoint, suggesting cleaner PRS contribution, though it is trained on a relatively small DEV set (n=13,496) and the AUROC is modest. (2) PGS005113 has a strong reported OR=1.35 (tight CI) and large validation (n=48,603) with CKDGen development, but lacks PRS-comparable AUC/R² and is embedded in a proteomics/comorbidity context. (3) PGS004030 and (4) PGS004074 are next-best within the same five-biobank cluster (AUROC≈0.589; R²≈0.019) with covariates=0 and similar endpoints; differences among these siblings are small.

Main limitation lowering confidence: the strongest disease-focused CKD model (PGS002237) reports only covariate-heavy full-model AUROC (no PGS-only AUC/R²), while the cleaner-covariate five-biobank cluster reports modest AUROC/R²; without PRS-only metrics for PGS002237, the #1 vs. top runners-up remains somewhat uncertain.

Direct-match candidates are present (multiple COPD EFO-mapped models). The best-supported pick is PGS001783 because it is endpoint-aligned (phenotyping_reported: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS-auto; 884,139 variants), and reports a PRS-comparable metric (Nagelkerke R2 with covariates regressed out = 0.038092) that is consistent with the provided COPD heritability ceiling (h2_liability=0.0388), plus a reported AUROC=0.74 (not treated as PRS-only). Key limitation: it comes from a global biobank framework-style paper and has small validation n (7,128), so external benchmark rank-#1 is not assured.

Runners-up: PGS001788 is the closest sibling (same paper/method/endpoint) with much larger validation n (337,168) but materially weaker PRS-comparable R2 (0.0163). Among the UKB sparse snpnet models with explicit PGS-only AUROC/R2, PGS001332 (exact COPD label) is preferred over PGS001334/PGS001333 due to endpoint fidelity and slightly stronger full-model AUROC; however, all snpnet models show weak PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC ~0.54–0.55; PGS-only R2 ~0.002–0.003) and are penalized as pan-trait sparse framework scores. Other direct matches (PGS001850/PGS002062 portability partial-r; PGS004466/PGS004536 effect-size-only with unknown covariates) are less supported from the visible evidence for top-5 safety versus the selected set.

All 6 candidates are direct matches to the target concept (cirrhosis of liver) via trait_efo/phenotyping, but several are alcohol-specific subtypes, which is a partial endpoint mismatch for a generic cirrhosis target. PGS004621 is best supported because it is explicitly for cirrhosis (trait_efo and phenotyping_reported both ‘Cirrhosis’), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS) with very large variant count (1,089,806), and has exceptionally large validation (n=1,153,995) with basic covariates (age/sex/PCs), which together provide stronger top-5 safety than sparse GWAS-hit scores. However, confidence is limited because the only reported discrimination is a full-model AUROC (~0.68) without PRS-only metrics, making cross-model performance comparability weak per the provided domain guidance.

Runners-up: PGS000726 is the closest same-trait ‘Cirrhosis’ model with multi-cohort development and moderate per-SD OR (1.32) plus a top-vs-bottom quintile OR (2.26), but it is a 12-variant GWS score and lacks AUC/R2. PGS000704 is alcohol-specific but methodologically strong (snpnet multi-PRS; 183k variants) with a reasonable full-model C-index (0.711) and HR per SD 1.18, though the endpoint is alcoholic cirrhosis (subtype). PGS000776 has an endpoint description that is less clean for generic cirrhosis (incident/time-to-event in an at-risk NAFLD context) and is a 9-variant score despite a similar full-model C-index (0.677). ontology: congenital vitamin k-dependent coagulation factors deficiency
rationale:
Two direct-match candidates are present (PGS001826, PGS002034) and both are endpoint-aligned: trait_efo matches the target and phenotyping_reported/trait_reported are the same (“Congenital deficiency of other clotting factors (including factor VII)”). They come from the same portability-framework publication, with the same training cohort (UKB), training size (n=391,124), covariates (basic demographics + PCs), evaluation ancestry mix, and the same validation sample size (n=19,864), so study-context signals do not separate them. Performance evidence is also essentially tied: both report nearly identical partial correlation (0.0562 vs 0.0563) with overlapping CIs, and no PRS-only AUC/R2 is available to differentiate.

Given the domain-knowledge fallback when PRS-only AUC is absent, method/structure becomes the main differentiator. PGS002034 uses LDpred2 (genome-wide shrinkage) with many more variants (32,552 vs 45), which is a positive structural signal for capturing polygenic signal and is therefore the safer top-5 choice under ambiguity. However, because both candidates are near-clones with indistinguishable reported performance and both originate from a portability framework (a known weaker archetype for external generalization), the overall direct-match recommendation remains low-confidence and thus DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL.

Two direct-match candidates are present (both map to corneal dystrophy with matching trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported) and come from the same UK Biobank portability publication with identical training cohort (UKB), training size (n=391,124), covariates (basic demographics + PCs), ancestry distribution, and validation sample size (n=19,321). With endpoint fidelity and transportability context effectively tied, the main differentiator in visible evidence is the selected PRS-comparable metric: PGS002042 reports a higher partial correlation (partial-r=0.0471, CI 0.033–0.0611) than PGS001835 (0.0384, CI 0.0243–0.0525), and it uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with many more variants (59,944 vs 38), which is a supportive structural signal when other fields are similar. Outcome is DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL (not high-quality) because both candidates are from a portability/framework-style study and neither provides stronger PRS-comparable metrics like PGS-only AUROC/R2 or effect sizes; the evidence base is therefore limited and the performance gap is modest with overlapping CIs.

Direct-match candidates are present (many models with trait_efo=coronary artery disease). PGS003725 is best supported on visible evidence because it has strong endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported: coronary artery disease), a disease-focused multi-ancestry study archetype (Nat Med; multi-ancestry GWAS and multi-cohort development), and strong PRS signal via effect sizes (HR=1.75; OR=2.14), which domain guidance treats as highly informative when PRS-only AUC/R2 are absent. However, the overall decision remains sub-optimal because most candidates (including PGS003725) lack clearly PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC/R2), making cross-model performance ranking uncertain and forcing reliance on effect sizes and study context.

Runners-up: PGS002244 is a strong disease-focused, large multi-ancestry evaluation (Cell Genom; EVAL n=343,676) with supportive OR=1.64 but weaker than PGS003725’s effect sizes. PGS000013 is a classic CAD LDpred genome-wide score with explicit PGS-only R2=0.04 (useful comparable metric) and large validation (n=288,978), but its key reported AUROC is full-model and thus discounted. PGS000018 shows very high full-model AUROC (0.89) but is based on prevalent CAD with very small validation (n=3,309) and no PRS-only metrics, increasing risk that the AUROC is not PRS-driven. PGS001780 reports very high full-model AUROC (0.913) but includes questionnaire/risk-factor integration context (publication framing) and lacks PRS-only metrics, so it is treated cautiously despite large validation (n=291,720).

Direct-match candidates are present (all map to Crohn disease with phenotype fields consistent with Crohn’s disease endpoints), but the evidence is mixed across study archetypes and metric comparability, so the overall direct-match decision is sub-optimal.

PGS004254 is best supported because it is a direct Crohn’s disease score with a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2-auto; 744,682 variants) and reports a strong effect size signal (OR=2.18, 95% CI 2.05–2.32) plus a high AUROC=0.72 in European evaluation with only basic covariates (age, sex, PCs). However, its reported AUROC appears to be a full-model metric (no PGS-only AUROC/R² provided), so the PRS-only contribution cannot be cleanly compared against the snpnet framework scores; this limits confidence.

Among the remaining direct matches, PGS001331 and PGS001330 come from a known pan-trait UK Biobank sparse framework (“across 813 traits”), which domain guidance flags as a systematic external-validation weakness despite having explicit PRS-only metrics. Between those two siblings, PGS001331 is the stronger runner-up because it has slightly better PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC 0.579 vs 0.576; PGS-only R² 0.00677 vs 0.00621; incremental AUROC 0.027 vs 0.024) with essentially identical covariates and validation size/ancestry. PGS001330 ranks behind due to weaker PRS-only metrics and an additional endpoint nuance (time-to-event phenotype), which domain guidance treats as a mild negative when competing against a standard disease endpoint.

Direct-match candidates for dementia are present (e.g., PGS005170, PGS000929, PGS000946, PGS001827, PGS002035, PGS004281–PGS004284, PGS004318), so outcome is not NO_MATCH_FOUND. PGS005170 is best supported because it has strong endpoint fidelity to the target (phenotyping_reported: incident all-cause dementia; trait_efo: dementia), uses an explicitly integrative multi-PRS construction (method: integrative PRS of 24 component PRSs), and reports a directly comparable discrimination metric (AUROC=0.761) with basic covariates including APOE dosage and PCs; it also has substantial multi-ancestry evaluation representation (EVAL includes AFR/AMR/EAS/EUR) and many performance records (record_count=18), suggesting more robust evidence than single-record dementia models. Main limitation: its training and validation sample sizes shown are relatively small (~2k each) compared with several UKB-based dementia models, and the AUROC is a full-model metric (no explicit PGS-only AUROC/R2), so the PRS-only contribution is uncertain.

Runners-up: (1) PGS000823 remains strong on endpoint fidelity (incident all-cause dementia) with a large validation sample (n=12,978) and a sizable HR contrast (top vs bottom third HR=1.36), but lacks PRS-only metrics. (2–4) PGS004281/PGS004282/PGS004284 are exact all-cause dementia endpoints with large UKB evaluation (n=67,428) and high reported full-model AUROC (~0.818–0.819) under basic covariates; however, they are single-record and provide no PRS-only metrics, making their apparent advantage potentially covariate-driven and less benchmark-safe than the integrative dementia-focused model. Pan-trait snpnet dementia models (PGS000929/PGS000946) and portability-framework dementia models (PGS001827/PGS002035) are deprioritized per the provided domain guidance due to framework-origin penalties despite having explicit PGS-only metrics/partial-r, because disease-focused alternatives with acceptable endpoint fidelity exist.

Direct-match candidates are present (multiple MDD/depression PGS). The strongest visible cluster is the set of near-clone, endpoint-faithful MDD models from the same 2023 “Phenotype integration improves power…” study (PGS003576–PGS003585): they share a direct MDD phenotype (phenotyping_reported: major depressive disorder), consistent EUR GWAS/DEV with multi-ancestry evaluation, and report comparable R² values in the ~0.018–0.026 range. Within that coherent family, PGS003578 has the highest reported R² (0.0257) with the larger validation sample size (n=42,250) compared with the similarly high PGS003580 (R²=0.0254; n=42,250), making PGS003578 the best-supported pick from the visible evidence.

Runners-up were ranked by remaining direct-match support: (1) PGS003580 is essentially tied within the same strong family but with slightly lower R²; (2) PGS003576 has slightly lower R² (0.0241) but same endpoint/study context; (3) PGS004760 is a modern integrative method (PRSmixPlus) with a clean incremental R² (0.024) but smaller evaluation (n=9,462) and less corroborating family context; (4) PGS003333 is endpoint-faithful (MDD) with multi-cohort training listed and moderate pseudo-R² (0.022) but has unknown covariates.

Overall outcome is DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL (not high-quality) because across the full candidate list there is no consistently reported PRS-only AUROC/R² metric, many metrics are full-model or heterogeneous, and at least one candidate shows implausible/likely non-comparable variance explained reporting (e.g., PGS000907 ‘Variance explained (Nagelkerke’s R2*100)=0.77’ on a non-disease endpoint), which increases uncertainty about cross-study metric comparability even though the chosen family itself is internally consistent.

All 8 candidates are direct matches to dilated cardiomyopathy by trait_efo, with generally coherent endpoint phrasing. The strongest-supported primary pick is PGS004862 because it is an MTAG-enhanced DCM score (domain guidance mildly prefers MTAG siblings within the same study family), has the best reported discrimination among the two large-EUR-evaluated siblings from the same Nat Genet paper (full-model AUROC 0.71 vs 0.70; OR 1.76 vs 1.56), and is evaluated in a very large European sample (n=347,585) with only basic covariates (age, age^2, sex, PCs). However, the overall decision remains sub-optimal because none of the candidates report clearly PRS-only AUROC/R²; most reported AUROC/R² appear to be full-model or otherwise not explicitly PRS-comparable, limiting confidence in cross-model performance ranking.

Runner-up ordering: PGS004861 is the closest sibling to the best model with nearly identical design but slightly weaker AUROC/OR. Among the 2024-12-16 Nat Genet family, PGS004951 is preferred next because it is MTAG and shows stronger univariate (PRS-only) AUC (0.67) and OR (1.93) than its clinical non-MTAG sibling (PGS004950), albeit with small validation n=7,761. PGS004949 is next with strong univariate AUC (0.68) and the largest OR (1.91) among the non-ischemic DCM MTAG models, though its evaluation is MAE-only (transportability uncertainty) and metrics are not directly comparable to the large-EUR-evaluated pair. PGS004947 follows as another MTAG non-ischemic DCM model with solid univariate AUC (0.66) and OR (1.73), but similarly MAE-only evaluation and smaller n=96,016. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All 5 candidates are direct matches to diverticular disease (trait_efo/phenotyping_reported align to diverticular disease/K57, with one including diverticulitis). For likely external-benchmark #1 performance, PGS004614 is best supported because it comes from a disease-focused diverticular disease study (Cell Genom; not a pan-trait framework), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (SBayesR) with ~1.08M variants, and reports strong full-model discrimination (AUROC=0.76, EUR eval). Main limitation: it lacks PRS-only/comparable metrics (no PGS-only AUROC/R2) and uses family history as a covariate, so the reported AUROC may be covariate-inflated and not directly comparable.

Runners-up: PGS000997 has explicit PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.591, PGS-only R2=0.0178) and a larger validation sample, but it is from a known pan-trait UKB framework ("across 813 traits" snpnet), which domain guidance flags as typically underperforming disease-focused scores in external validation. Between the two Commun Biol integration-study models, PGS004544 is ranked above PGS004474 due to slightly higher reported per-SD OR (1.321 vs 1.312) with otherwise near-identical endpoint/method/variant count and similarly missing AUC/R2. PGS000996 is last because it is also a pan-trait framework snpnet score and has weaker PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.552; PGS-only R2=0.0037) and a broader phenotype including diverticulitis.

All three candidates are direct matches to the target (same EFO: Dupuytren Contracture; phenotyping_reported aligns). The strongest visible head-to-head evidence comes from the two same-publication portability-framework siblings (Am J Hum Genet “Portability of 245 polygenic scores…”), where PGS002092 (LDpred2, 484,484 variants) has slightly higher PRS-comparable performance evidence (partial-r 0.0797, CI 0.0655–0.0938) than PGS001880 (penalized regression, 2,443 variants; partial-r 0.0783, CI 0.0641–0.0924), and also has the stronger genome-wide shrinkage structure and much larger variant count—both supportive when endpoints/covariates are otherwise similar. PGS001254 reports explicit AUROC/R2 including PGS-only metrics, but it is from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework (“across 813 traits”) with an extremely small variant set (11 SNPs), which domain guidance flags as a common external-generalization weakness; its reported full-model AUROC is also not a reliable substitute for PRS-only ranking. Main limitation: none of the portability-framework candidates report AUROC/R2 here (only partial-r), and all models are UKB-derived frameworks rather than clearly disease-focused multi-cohort Dupuytren studies, so the #1 choice is not strongly locked despite PGS002092 being the best-supported within the visible set.

All 4 candidates are direct-match by trait_efo=follicular lymphoma, but endpoint fidelity and PRS-comparable performance evidence are uneven. PGS002304 has the cleanest phenotype alignment (trait_reported and phenotyping_reported both “Follicular lymphoma”) and the strongest reported discrimination signal in the visible set (full_model AUROC=0.61, European eval), albeit with very small validation_sample_size (n=197) and no PRS-only metrics/covariates detail (covariates unknown), so its apparent edge could be unstable. Among the PRSweb siblings, PGS000644 (lassosum; 2,209,179 variants) slightly outperforms PGS000643 (PRS-CS; 1,048,780 variants) on the same evaluation context (both EUR; same covariates age/sex/batch/PCs; same validation n=3,256) with marginally higher full_model AUROC (0.538 vs 0.532) and higher pseudo-R² (0.00349 vs 0.00282), making it the safer runner-up cluster. PGS003455 is penalized despite large validation n=20,134 because phenotyping_reported is explicitly mismatched (“Chronic lymphocytic leukemia”) and it lacks comparable discrimination metrics (only a weak per-SD OR ~1.07 with CI crossing 1), making its direct-match support fragile. Overall, the best choice is sub-optimal because none report PRS-only AUROC/R² and the top candidate’s validation is very small while the larger-validated PRSweb models have weaker full-model discrimination and non-exact phenotype labels (“Nodular lymphoma”).

All 15 candidates are direct matches to glaucoma or its dominant clinical subtype POAG (via trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported). The strongest overall evidence package for likely external benchmark performance is PGS001792: it targets POAG, uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS-auto) with very large variant count (911,402), and reports supportive PRS-comparable signal (Nagelkerke R2 with covariates regressed out = 0.03209) plus a strong full-model AUROC (0.777) in a very large evaluation sample (n=347,396). Its covariates are basic (age/sex/PCs), reducing concern that the AUROC is driven by heavy clinical leakage. Main limitation: the reported AUROC is a full-model metric (not explicitly PGS-only), and several other candidates have similarly strong-looking evidence, so the #1 choice is not unambiguous.

Runners-up: PGS004944 has very large validation (n=407,667) and strong OR (1.74) with a competitive full-model AUROC (0.748), but its endpoint is self-reported POAG and evaluation is MAE-only, which adds transport/endpoint uncertainty. PGS001797 is a close sibling to PGS001792 (PRS-CS-auto, genome-wide, PRS-comparable R2=0.031479) but has much smaller validation (n=7,128) and lower full-model AUROC (0.749). PGS002043 (LDpred2) has the best partial-r among the UKB portability family (0.0458) and a large genome-wide model, but it comes from a portability framework study (penalized vs disease-focused) and lacks clearer PRS-only metrics. PGS004766 (PRSmixPlus) has an explicit incremental R2=0.031 with basic covariates, but has smaller validation (n=9,462) and limited supporting records (record_count=1), making its external top-5 safety less certain than the global-biobank PRS-CS models.

Direct-match candidates for gout are present. PGS004160 is best supported as a standalone gout PRS in this visible set because it is an explicit gout endpoint (phenotyping_reported: Gout), uses an ensemble-style MultiPRS method (UKBB-EUR.MultiPRS.CV; domain knowledge: multi-score aggregation is a strong structural positive), reports strong full-model discrimination (AUROC 0.6936) alongside a relatively high reported R² (0.0893), and is evaluated in a reasonably sized EUR validation (n=90,274) with no added covariates listed (covariates: 0), reducing concern that performance is mainly covariate-driven. Key limitation: the reported AUROC/R² appear to be full-model metrics (not explicitly PGS-only), so cross-model comparability is imperfect and lowers confidence.

Runners-up were ranked by remaining direct-match support emphasizing (i) endpoint fidelity, (ii) presence/strength of PRS-comparable metrics (incremental R² or PRS-only metrics), and (iii) structural method strength and validation context. PGS004768 (PRSmixPlus) is a strong alternative due to a large-variant integrative method and the largest incremental R² reported (0.081) but has a much smaller validation sample (n=9,462) and lacks AUROC/PGS-only metrics. PGS004047 (LDpred2.CV) and PGS004018 (lassosum.CV) are strong within the coherent five-biobank method-comparison family (same endpoint, covariates: 0, same validation n=90,274) with the best full-model AUROC/R² among those siblings (0.685/0.080 and 0.678/0.073, respectively), but they are single-method (non-ensemble) and trail PGS004160 on the reported metrics. PGS004265 (GenoBoost) has high full-model AUROC (~0.798) but is from a different study context and the metric is not PGS-only; without incremental/PGS-only metrics it is harder to treat that AUROC as directly comparable, so it is kept as a lower-safety runner-up despite the high value.

All three visible candidates are direct matches to the target trait via trait_efo = "Hashimoto's thyroiditis" and share the same phenotyping_reported ("lymphocytic thyroiditis"), publication family (same medRxiv preprint), evaluation ancestry set, and identical validation sample size (n=94,651), so endpoint fidelity and transportability context do not separate them. None reports PRS-only AUROC/R2; only full-model AUROC is shown, which domain guidance says should not be treated as decisive for PRS ranking, so overall evidence quality is limited.

Within this near-clone set, PGS005271 is preferred because it has the strongest PRS-discrimination proxy in the visible evidence: OR per SD ≈ 1.55 (strong per the provided effect-size guidance) and it is a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRSCS) with ~1.085M variants, which is structurally favorable when endpoints are otherwise identical. PGS005270 has slightly higher full-model AUROC (0.639 vs 0.630) but a much weaker OR (~1.04) and a sparse P+T construction (55 variants), making it less likely to be the best standalone PRS despite the small AUROC edge. PGS005272 is also PRSCS genome-wide but has weaker full-model AUROC (0.605) and weaker OR (~1.42) than PGS005271, so it ranks behind it.

Main limitation: because all candidates lack PRS-only metrics and covariates are "Unknown", the ranking relies heavily on effect-size magnitude and method/variant-count structure within a single study family, leaving moderate residual uncertainty about which would top an external benchmark.

All listed candidates are direct matches to the target trait concept (heart failure / congestive heart failure), but the evidence is not cleanly decisive because many models report only full-model discrimination (C-index/AUROC) without explicit PRS-only AUROC/R2, and several come from framework/benchmarking-style publications where reported metrics may be less comparable across candidates.

Best pick: PGS005083 is selected because it is a direct CHF endpoint (PheCode 428.1), uses a modern genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS), and within the large same-endpoint sibling set from the same publication family it has the strongest visible combined performance/effect-size package: very high reported full-model C-index (0.75368) alongside a strong per-SD OR (1.455, 95% CI 1.38–1.54). This combination provides better top-5 safety than candidates with weaker OR/HR evidence or much lower discrimination.

Runners-up: PGS005077, PGS005076, PGS005084, and PGS005078 are ranked next because they share the same CHF endpoint and study family (reducing endpoint/design heterogeneity) and have similarly high C-index (~0.752–0.754) with strong ORs (~1.44–1.45). They remain close competitors to the best model based on the visible fields.

Main limitation lowering confidence/outcome: the top cluster (PGS005076/77/78/83/84 and related siblings) is effectively indistinguishable on endpoint and covariates, and all rely on full-model C-index rather than clearly PRS-only metrics; therefore the #1 choice is a moderate-confidence preference rather than a clearly dominant winner. Additionally, other direct-match candidates (e.g., PGS001790 with PRS-only R2 reported, and PGS005097 from a large multi-cohort disease-focused Nat Genet paper) could plausibly outperform in an external benchmark, but their visible metrics are not directly comparable to this CHF sibling cluster.

All 7 candidates are direct matches to hip osteoarthritis/coxarthrosis at the EFO level, but the pool has limited PRS-comparable performance reporting (most lack PGS-only AUROC/R²), so the #1 choice is not strongly locked.

PGS002763 is best-supported overall because it has high endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported: hip osteoarthritis), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS; 1,052,273 variants), and reports a relatively strong per-SD effect size (OR=1.38, 95% CI 1.31–1.46), which the provided domain guidance treats as meaningful discrimination evidence when AUC/R² are absent. Its covariates are basic/technical (age, sex, PCs, technical covariates), reducing concern that performance is covariate-driven.

Runners-up: (1) PGS004478 (LDpred2; genome-wide; OR≈1.296) and (2) PGS004548 (metaPRS-style aggregation; OR≈1.216) are endpoint-aligned coxarthrosis models from the same 2024 study family, but both have unknown covariates and only modest effect-size evidence, limiting confidence. (3) PGS002728 has strong endpoint relevance via total hip replacement and reports a full-model AUROC=0.66, but lacks PRS-only metrics and uses a treatment/procedure proxy endpoint rather than direct disease status. (4) PGS004882 has very large validation (n=412,090) and an incident hip OA endpoint with HR=1.4, but appears to come from an absolute-risk/incidence framework context and has a very small training sample (n=404) plus only a modest C-index (0.6), making its standalone PRS strength harder to trust.

Not selected as best: PGS000967 reports explicit PGS-only AUROC/R², but it is from a known pan-trait sparse UKB framework (snpnet; 634 variants; “across 813 traits”), which the provided domain knowledge flags as systematically underperforming disease-focused scores in external validation; its PRS-only AUROC (~0.56) is also modest and consistent with weak standalone signal.

Direct-match candidates for Hodgkin’s lymphoma are present (PGS000637/PGS000638/PGS000639/PGS000640 and PGS003449). Among the PRSweb Hodgkin’s disease sibling set (same publication, same endpoint wording, same EUR-only GWAS/DEV/EVAL, same covariates), PGS000639 (P+T, 20 variants) has the strongest visible validation performance: highest full-model AUROC (0.62) and highest Nagelkerke pseudo-R² (0.0276), plus the strongest per-SD effect size (OR 1.476, 95% CI 1.154–1.889). This coherent within-family advantage makes it the best-supported pick for likely top-1 benchmark performance while maintaining endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported: Hodgkin’s disease) and clean/basic covariates.

Main limitation: none of the Hodgkin’s lymphoma candidates report PRS-only AUROC/R²; the available AUROC/R² are full-model metrics (age/sex/PC/batch-adjusted), so cross-model comparability is limited and confidence cannot be high. PGS003449 is a direct-label match but has internally inconsistent phenotype metadata (phenotyping_reported shown as chronic lymphocytic leukemia) and weak effect size (OR ~1.02), reducing its top-5 safety despite large validation n. The remaining PRSweb siblings rank as runners-up based on descending AUROC/R²/effect-size support within the same endpoint/covariate context (PGS000638 > PGS000637 ≈ PGS000640).

Direct-match hypertension candidates are present. PGS004236 is best supported because it is explicitly hypertension (trait_efo=hypertension; phenotyping_reported=prevalent hypertension), comes from a disease-focused hypertension study (Nat Commun: multi-ethnic PRS associated with hypertension prevalence/progression), has multi-ethnic evaluation (listed as European/African American/Hispanic/Asian unspecified), and reports strong effect-size evidence (OR=2.1) alongside a high reported AUROC (0.764) under a clearly specified covariate set (demographics + PCs + BMI/smoking/site), giving a comparatively rich and coherent evidence package for external performance/top-5 safety. Runners-up: PGS004234 is a near-sibling from the same study with very similar AUROC (0.763) but lacks the strong OR evidence shown for PGS004236; PGS001320 (Hypertension, snpnet, PLoS Genet) provides explicit PRS-comparable metrics including PGS-only AUROC/R2 and incremental AUROC, but it is from a pan-trait sparse-PRS framework which domain guidance flags as typically underperforming disease-focused models; PGS002652 (Hypertension, PolyFun-pred, Nat Genet) has strong incremental R2 evidence (0.0539) but limited other comparable metrics shown; PGS004787 (Hypertension, PRSmixPlus) has strong incremental R2 (0.073) but is supported by a small evaluation sample (n=9,462) and lacks directly comparable AUROC/PRS-only metrics in the visible record. Main limitation: across the hypertension set, many candidates report only full-model AUROC or incremental R2 with differing covariates/endpoints (prevalent vs incident vs time-to-event), making cross-model performance comparability imperfect; thus confidence is moderate rather than high.

All 7 candidates are direct matches to the target hyperthyroidism concept via either thyrotoxicosis/hyperthyroidism endpoints (PGS001042/PGS001043/PGS001815/PGS002023) or the clinically dominant autoimmune subtype Graves’ disease (PGS005264/PGS005265/PGS005266), which the provided domain_knowledge explicitly treats as a strong direct match for a generic hyperthyroidism target when competing options are older UKB framework/portability scores. The main limitation is that these Graves’ models report only full-model AUROC with unknown covariates and lack PRS-only comparable metrics (no PGS-only AUROC/R²), so cross-model performance comparability is imperfect; meanwhile the UKB snpnet hyperthyroidism/thyrotoxicosis models (PGS001042/PGS001043) do provide PRS-only metrics but come from a pan-trait UKB framework paper that domain_knowledge flags as often underperforming disease-focused multi-cohort scores in external validation. Runners-up are ranked by remaining direct-match support: the near-identical PRSCS Graves’ sibling (PGS005266), then the P+T Graves’ model (PGS005264), then the two snpnet UKB hyperthyroidism/thyrotoxicosis models with very similar PRS-only AUC/R² (PGS001042 slightly ahead of PGS001043).

All 4 candidates are direct matches by trait_efo (hypertrophic cardiomyopathy). PGS004911 is best supported because it has strong endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported: hypertrophic cardiomyopathy), a modern genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS) with very large variant count (~374k), and the strongest visible performance package among the PRS-CS siblings (full-model AUROC 0.80; R² 0.048; OR/HR reported) in a large European evaluation (n=343,182). Domain guidance also mildly prefers MTAG-enhanced variants over base variants within the same disease family, making PGS004911 preferable to the otherwise near-clone PGS004910 (AUROC 0.73; R² 0.031). Main limitation: the reported AUROC/R² appear to be full-model metrics (not explicitly PGS-only), so cross-model comparability is imperfect and confidence is capped. Runners-up: PGS004910 is the closest sibling with the same endpoint/covariates but weaker metrics; PGS000739 has a high full-model AUROC (0.821) but uses heavier clinical covariates (risk factors + rare variant carrier status), making the AUROC less indicative of standalone PRS quality; PGS000778 has limited/unclear training info, non-reported validation ancestry, very small validation (n=368), and a more restricted endpoint (clinical events among pathogenic sarcomeric variant carriers), reducing general direct-match support.

All listed candidates are direct matches at the trait/EFO level, but they vary substantially in endpoint fidelity and in whether reported metrics are PRS-comparable. PGS005218 is best supported because it is a disease-focused hypothyroidism GWAS/PRS paper (Nat Genet) with a very large multi-cohort development set (n=1,146,562) and large validation (n=441,692), and it reports strong discrimination (full-model AUROC=0.859) with an incident hypothyroidism endpoint. However, its covariates include thyroid biomarkers (TSH, T4, anti-TPO), which are near-outcome predictors and can inflate full-model AUROC; no PGS-only AUROC/R2 is provided, so the magnitude of PRS-only contribution is uncertain—this keeps confidence at Moderate rather than High.

Runners-up were ranked by remaining direct-match support emphasizing endpoint fidelity and PRS-comparable evidence: (1) PGS000965 and (2) PGS001181 (both from the UKB 813-traits framework) provide explicit PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC ~0.689 and PGS-only R2 ~0.073–0.074) with large validation (n=67,425), but are penalized as pan-trait framework scores and thus less benchmark-safe than a disease-focused GWAS meta-analysis model. (3) PGS004935 reports AUROC=0.7 and OR=1.5 with a direct hypothyroidism endpoint, but has small validation (n=8,417) and unknown covariates, limiting comparability. (4) PGS002653 (PolyFun-pred) has modest incremental R2 (0.0262) in a methodologically strong Nat Genet cross-population PRS paper, but the reported metric is incremental/full-model context rather than PRS-only, and its incremental R2 is lower than the PRS-only R2 seen in the snpnet framework models. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

Two direct-match candidates are present (both map to the same trait_efo and phenotyping_reported: “Disorders of iron metabolism”) and come from the same UKB portability publication with identical training cohort (UKB), training size (n=391,124), covariates (basic demographics + PCs), validation size (n=19,883), and similar multi-ancestry evaluation distribution. With endpoint and study context effectively tied, the only visible differentiator is the selected European validation metric: PGS002031 has slightly higher partial correlation (partial-r 0.1355, CI 0.1219–0.1492) than PGS001823 (0.1307, CI 0.117–0.1444), so it is the best-supported pick. However, confidence is limited because both models lack PRS-comparable AUC/R2 and effect sizes, and the metric difference is small with overlapping CIs; additionally, both originate from a portability-style framework study, which domain guidance flags as less reliably top-performing in external benchmarks when stronger disease-focused alternatives exist (none are visible here).

All 4 candidates are direct-match within the juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA) disease family, from the same disease-focused publication (Ann Rheum Dis; “Genomic risk scores for juvenile idiopathic arthritis and its subtypes.”), with consistent EUR-only development/evaluation and similarly clean/basic covariates (sex, PCs 1–10). The key differentiator for a generic target_trait = “juvenile idiopathic arthritis” is endpoint fidelity: PGS000114 is the only model whose trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported are the umbrella JIA diagnosis rather than a specific subtype, making it the most faithful direct match for broad JIA risk.

However, the evidence is not high-quality for picking a clear #1 on PRS performance because none of the models report PRS-only AUROC/R2; the available AUROCs are full-model metrics (even if only lightly covariate-adjusted), which domain guidance says should not be treated as decisive. Subtype models show higher full-model AUROC (notably PGS000324 AUROC 0.93) and stronger ORs, but they are endpoint-mismatched to the umbrella trait and may not generalize to overall JIA. Among runners-up, PGS000325 and PGS000326 are ranked ahead of PGS000324 primarily on closer conceptual proximity to general JIA (more common/broader JIA categories than enthesitis-related) despite PGS000324’s higher reported full-model AUROC; validation sizes are treated as weak tie-breakers only.

All 10 listed candidates are direct matches to the target trait (kidney cancer / renal carcinoma / renal cell carcinoma; RCC is explicitly noted in the provided domain knowledge as the clinically dominant subtype of kidney cancer). PGS004908 is best supported because it combines strong endpoint alignment (phenotyping_reported: Kidney cancer), the strongest visible PRS-discrimination signal via effect size (OR per SD=1.5, 95% CI 1.43–1.58; domain guidance treats OR≥1.5 as strong), and the highest reported AUROC among the pool (0.74, though this is a full-model metric and cannot be treated as PGS-only). It also comes from a disease-focused GWAS publication (Nat Genet) with large European evaluation (n=324,805) and standard epidemiologic covariates (age/sex/PCs/BMI/smoking/hypertension), which are not flagged as heavy leakage in the domain policy.

Key limitation: none of the candidates report explicit PRS-only AUROC/R², so ranking relies on effect sizes plus non-PRS-only full-model AUROC and study/endpoint coherence; this keeps confidence below High. Runners-up are ranked by remaining direct-match support: PGS000076 and PGS000787 are endpoint-faithful incident kidney cancer models with large EUR evaluation (~391k) and similar full-model AUROC (~0.722) plus modest HR (~1.15–1.16); PGS000722 has weaker AUROC (0.567) but strong endpoint fidelity and large evaluation (~401k); PGS004690 uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (AnnoPred; structurally favorable) with large training (n=367,502) but shows only modest AUROC (0.5644) and smaller evaluation (n=40,841).

Direct-match candidates for the target trait (kidney failure) are present, including PGS004562 and PGS004492 (trait_efo=kidney failure; phenotyping_reported=N18 chronic renal failure) and PGS000708 (trait_reported=Kidney failure but phenotyping_reported=Diabetic kidney failure in all). Best-supported pick is PGS004562 because it is endpoint-aligned to kidney failure (N18 chronic renal failure) and shows the strongest per-SD effect size among the kidney-failure-labeled options (OR=1.39548 vs 1.17083 for PGS004492), with a genome-wide method and large variant count (1,059,939). However, overall evidence quality is limited because these kidney-failure models from the same publication family report no PRS-comparable metrics (no PGS-only AUROC/R2; no incremental metrics) and have unknown covariates, so external-benchmark ranking remains uncertain. Runners-up are ranked by remaining direct-match support and top-5 safety: PGS002237 is a very strong near-direct kidney-failure spectrum endpoint (CKD stage 3+; eGFR<45) from a disease-focused Nat Med study with strong AUROC (0.78) and OR (1.47) and multi-ancestry evaluation; PGS004158 is a coherent CKD/dialysis endpoint with the best AUROC among the five-biobank CKD family (0.5917) but is not kidney-failure-specific; PGS000708 is kidney-failure-labeled but restricted to diabetic kidney failure subtype and its reported C-index (0.779) is full-model with limited PRS-isolated evidence; PGS004492 is the other kidney-failure-specific N18 model but with weaker effect size than PGS004562.

All 7 candidates are direct matches to knee osteoarthritis by trait_efo/phenotyping_reported, but the pool has limited PRS-comparable metrics (most lack PGS-only AUROC/R²), so the #1 choice is not decisively supported.

Best pick (PGS002767): Strongest visible PRS-discrimination signal via effect size (OR=1.35 per SD, CI 1.3–1.4) on an explicitly matched endpoint (“Knee osteoarthritis”), using a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS) with very large variant count (~1.05M) and EUR evaluation (n=39,444). This combination aligns with domain guidance favoring endpoint fidelity plus strong effect-size evidence when PGS-only AUC/R² are absent.

Main limitation: PGS002767 provides no PRS-only AUROC/R² and only one performance record, so benchmark-top-1 certainty is constrained; comparisons against candidates reporting AUROC/C-index are not strictly PRS-comparable.

Runners-up rationale (ranked):
1) PGS002729: Exact endpoint (“Clinical osteoarthritis” for knee OA) and reports full-model AUROC=0.66 (CI 0.61–0.71) with mild covariates (Age, sex, BMI) and broad multi-cohort development; however AUROC is full-model (not PGS-only) and the score is only 24 GWAS-significant variants, which is structurally weaker for a polygenic trait.
2) PGS004549: Same knee OA endpoint family (M17 gonarthrosis), large variant count (~1.06M) and an explicit multi-score aggregation method (RFDiseasemetaPRS; domain knowledge says ensembling is a positive structural signal) with OR=1.3667, but covariates are unknown and effect size lacks CI.
3) PGS004479: Same publication/endpoint family as PGS004549 but single-score LDpred2 with slightly lower OR (1.3233) and unknown covariates.
4) PGS004883: Endpoint is aligned (“Incident knee osteoarthritis”) and reports C-index=0.60 plus HR=1.37 (CI 1.3–1.44), but it is packaged in an incidence/country-incidence framework context and shows an unusually small training sample (n=404) with development cohort listed as 1000G, which weakens confidence in robustness versus the more standard disease-PRS constructions above.

All 5 candidates are direct matches by trait_reported/trait_efo to late-onset Alzheimer’s disease, so the decision hinges on endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported), PRS-comparable performance evidence (effect sizes / PRS-only metrics), and transportability context.

Best pick (PGS000054): From the same disease-focused publication family as PGS000053 (“Polygenic risk scores in familial Alzheimer disease.”), with a clear per-SD effect size reported (OR=1.73, 95% CI 1.57–1.93), which is strong discriminative evidence per the provided domain guidance (OR≥1.5). Endpoint remains a direct disease endpoint (familial late-onset LOAD) with only basic covariates (age, sex). Although evaluation ancestry is AMR (Hispanic/Latin American) rather than EUR, the strong OR and clean endpoint/covariate framing make it the most compelling single piece of PRS-quality evidence in the visible set.

Main limitation / why not HIGH_QUALITY: No candidate reports a clearly PRS-only AUC/R²; several have missing/unclear covariates; and one candidate (PGS000334) reports a high R²=0.191 from a C+T pipeline with unknown covariates, which the domain document flags as potentially non-comparable/suspect. This makes the #1 ranking uncertain.

Runner-up ordering rationale: (1) PGS000053 is the closest sibling to the winner with the same endpoint/covariates and EUR evaluation, but has only moderate OR evidence (OR=1.29). (2) PGS000334 has a direct endpoint and reports R²=0.191, but that magnitude with C+T + unknown covariates triggers the provided heritability/metric-sanity warning, lowering top-5 safety. (3) PGS004918 reports only a full-model AUROC=0.731 on a very small evaluation (n=136) and uses a pathway-restricted 8-SNP construction, so the AUROC is not PRS-comparable and evidence is fragile. (4) PGS002289 has very large validation size but its phenotyping_reported is a cognition-by-age interaction outcome rather than a direct LOAD diagnosis endpoint, weakening endpoint fidelity despite the trait label.

Direct-match candidates for lung cancer are present (multiple models with trait_reported/phenotyping_reported as lung cancer or near-synonymous lung/bronchus cancer). Best-supported pick is PGS000078 because it has strong endpoint fidelity (incident lung cancer), very large European evaluation sample (n=392,539), and reports effect size (HR=1.16, 95% CI 1.11–1.22) alongside high full-model discrimination (AUROC 0.846; C-index 0.849). However, confidence is limited because the reported AUROC/C-index are full-model metrics with a heavy covariate set (includes family history, PM2.5, detailed smoking terms and interactions), and no PGS-only AUROC/R2 is provided, so the PRS contribution cannot be cleanly separated. Runners-up: PGS000789 is essentially the same 109-variant score evaluated in a similar large setting with similar metrics (also covariate-heavy), making it a close competitor; PGS004860 reports very high AUROC (0.893) but is single-cohort case-control with modest validation size (n=24,012) and still lacks PRS-only metrics; PGS000740 has large validation (n=167,955) but targets an endpoint-restricted phenotype (early onset <50) and is framed as absolute-risk trajectory packaging; PGS000721 is endpoint-faithful but has much smaller validation (n=1,202) and only full-model AUROC (0.738).

Direct-match candidates are present (12 models mapping to lupus erythematosus / systemic lupus erythematosus), but most report only full-model AUROC or non-comparable metrics and several have endpoint/covariate issues, so the best choice is not unequivocal.

Its main limitation is endpoint restriction (early-onset SLE, onset <20) and the fact that the AUROC is full-model (no PGS-only AUROC/R2), so benchmark performance for generic lupus erythematosus risk could differ.

Framework/portability scores (PGS001870, PGS002082) are direct-label matches to “lupus erythematosus” but come from a UKB portability framework and only report small partial correlations; given the presence of multiple disease-focused SLE candidates, they are not ranked in the top 5 for likely external benchmark performance.

Direct-match candidates are present (multiple models mapped to lymphoid leukemia / lymphocytic leukemia / chronic lymphocytic leukemia). PGS000788 is best supported on the visible evidence because it targets an incident lymphocytic leukemia endpoint (phenotyping_reported matches the target concept closely), is evaluated in a very large European cohort (n=391,338), and shows stronger reported discrimination/effect size than the closest sibling (full-model AUROC 0.738; HR 1.7) while using only basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs). However, confidence is limited because the reported AUROC/C-index are full-model metrics (no PGS-only AUROC/R2), and PGS000788 is explicitly derived from PGS000077 with inverse weights, creating uncertainty about whether the apparent improvement reflects PRS quality versus modeling/packaging differences. Runners-up: PGS000077 is the direct progenitor with similar endpoint/covariates and large evaluation (AUROC 0.719; HR 1.45). Among chronic lymphocytic leukemia models, PGS000648 and PGS000646 have the strongest within-family performance signals (AUROC ~0.696 and OR ~2.1 with higher pseudo-R2 ~0.10) but are subtype-shifted from the broader target and have much smaller validation (n~756). All 7 candidates are direct matches to macular degeneration/age-related macular degeneration by trait_reported/trait_efo, but endpoint fidelity and PRS-comparable performance evidence vary. Runners-up: (1) PGS004607 is a same-publication sibling with the same endpoint/covariates/method family but lower reported AUROC (0.65) and weaker OR per SD (1.48 vs 1.76), so it is the closest alternative but less supported. (3–4) PGS001834 and PGS002041 are portability-framework UKB-derived scores with only weak partial-correlation metrics (0.0175 and 0.0159) and less disease-focused study archetype; between them, PGS001834 is slightly better supported by the higher partial-r. All 7 visible candidates are direct matches to multiple sclerosis by trait_efo and phenotyping_reported, but the evidence is heterogeneous and often lacks PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC/R²). Direct-match candidates for myocardial infarction are present (multiple models with trait_efo/phenotyping_reported as myocardial infarction or acute myocardial infarction). Two direct-match candidates are present (both map to nicotine dependence via trait_efo and report the same endpoint label/phenotyping_reported: Tobacco use disorder) and come from the same UKB portability framework publication with identical training cohort (UKB), training size (n=391,124), covariates (basic demographics + PCs), and validation sample size (n=19,400).
